scope_note: SG-MA-PROFESSIONAL-CONDUCT after corrections following the V10L audit. The section keeps what the URAMP guidance manual says about licence status (non-disciplinary restriction, meaning no practice, from application; unchanged on enrolment; current on successful completion) and now adds that participation need not keep a licensee out of practice for the whole agreement: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 65G(d)(2)(iv) has the evaluation committee recommend whether the participant may continue or resume practice within the full scope of the licence, and the proviso at the end of s. 65G(e) makes any restriction on practice, or change to one, subject to licensing board approval; the manual (read 2026-09-17) describes the usual course, credited to the manual, of privileges restored during participation (normally after six months of compliance under a substance use disorder agreement, or a period set individually for mental health), under a supervisor agreement with quarterly reports, with a return to practice sent to the licensing board for final approval. Changed: orientation[14] (pinpoint now the s. 65G(e) proviso instead of s. 65G(g)), orientation[15], comparison_tables[3].rows[4], timing_deadlines[2] and a new [4], retrieval_prompts[25] and a new [26], quick_review[21] and a new [22], role_duties[11], worked_examples[5].steps[3] and a new common_traps[21]. New rule: MA-URAMP-PROGRAM-RETURN-TO-PRACTICE (the guidance manual, OFFICIAL_POLICY_VERIFIED). Scope gate: every actionable signal declined, for the reasons recorded at the previous freeze: 247 CMR 9.01 paragraphs and 247 CMR 2.00 definitions placed in other sections, and MA-URAMP, the record this section replaced. All six practice links stay.
